blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY — Thousands of students in Negros Occidental province just stayed home on Tuesday, Nov. 3, with the cancellation of face-to face classes due to expected elevated heat levels. On Tuesday morning, the state weather bureau forecast the heat index in the province to reach 41 degrees Celsius. The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction Management Office said such heat index falls under the “extreme caution” category, where heat cramps and heat exhaustion are possible, while continued heat exposure and physical activity may lead to heat stroke.
